subject: ACME POC — integration plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: ACME POC — integration plan & success criteria

Hi Ben / team,

Great to meet you all today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and a proposed POC plan so we have shared success criteria and clear next steps.

Summary of what we heard (from today's discovery):
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood as the inference runtime to power ACME's in-product assistant (document summarization + tool calling to internal search).
- Key constraints: sub-200ms median token latency for short prompts, end-to-end privacy (no customer data stored), and cost target roughly ~30% below current provider.

Proposed POC scope (2-4 week hands-on):
1) Integration: ACME devs call Redwood's hosted API from a staging environment (we'll provide test keys). We recommend SDK integration for streaming token responses and webhooks for tool-calls.
2) Workloads: 3 representative flows — short summarization (avg 150 tokens), multi-turn chat (tool calling to internal search), and batch embedding generation for indexing.
3) Success criteria (pass/fail):
   - Latency: median per-token latency <= 200ms for streaming chat under 95th percentile traffic of your test harness.
   - Correctness: tool-calling reliability >= 98% on deterministic prompts (we'll provide test set).
   - Cost: projected per-invocation token cost <= target budget (we'll run a billing simulation).

Owner / roles:
- ACME: Ben (product), Samir (eng owner)
- Redwood: Marissa (Sales PM), Neha (Solutions Engineer, will lead integration), Rishi (SRE & performance tuning)

Next steps / timeline:
- Today: I attached a draft POC plan (redwood-poc-mplan-v2.pdf) and the security Q&A you requested.
- Wed 2/26: ACME to confirm target test dataset and pick 2 devs for integration.
- Mon 3/1: Redwood to share integration checklist and sample SDK snippet for streaming + tool calling.
- Week of 3/8: ACME runs 2-week test; Redwood provides observability hooks and a weekly sync.

Attachments: redwood-poc-mplan-v2.pdf (high-level plan), acme-security-qna.xlsx (security answers).

Please reply with any adjustments to scope or timeline. If this looks good I will loop in Neha and Rishi to propose the specific SDK routes and a sample streaming implementation.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from the engineering side: 

1) Streaming & tool calling: our in-product assistant needs streaming partial tokens to the UI (so UX shows partial answers) and deterministic tool calls to internal search. Can you confirm the SDK supports:
   - token-level streaming over HTTP/WS;
   - tool-calling webhooks with guaranteed at-least-once delivery and idempotency keys?

2) Auth model: we need short-lived keys issued from our backend with KMS integration. Is that supported in the hosted POC flow or do we need a private deployment?

3) Logging/PII: We need clarity that logs won't contain PII and that KV cache is optional and can be disabled for the POC.

Samir — can you confirm which two devs will own the integration? We aim to start the dev work next week (3/1) if everything checks out.

-Ben

Hi Ben / Samir — looping in Neha and Rishi to map the implementation steps and give concrete SDK/API snippets. Below is a concise integration checklist and a sample flow you can hand to your devs.

Integration checklist (recommended minimal implementation for POC):
- Auth: backend mTLS or short-lived JWTs with KMS signing. For hosted POC we will issue scoped keys that expire; we can demonstrate KMS integration in a follow-up if needed.
- SDK: Use Redwood JavaScript SDK (node) for quick integration. Sample pseudo-snippet attached.
- Streaming: Use the /v1/stream endpoint over WebSocket for token-level streaming; fallback to SSE if you prefer.
- Tool calling: Define tool schema on our side (tool id, input schema). Redwood will POST a tool-call webhook to your /api/redwood/tools with an idempotency_key. Webhook retries: exponential backoff, 4 attempts.
- KV cache: disabled by default for POC; we will provide a cache-free execution profile.
- Observability: add X-Request-Id header from client; we will show per-request tracing and a token-latency dashboard.

Sample SDK snippet (JS, simplified):

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_POC_KEY });

// streaming example
const ws = client.stream({ model: 'redwood-13b', route: '/v1/stream' });
ws.on('token', t => ui.append(t));
ws.on('done', () => console.log('complete'));

// tool call: service posts tool result back to your webhook
// on our side we include idempotency_key header and tool_call_id

Attachments: sample-sdk-snippet.txt attached in the plan PDF.

Next concrete items this week:
- Tue 3/2: Redwood to share the SDK repo link + sample integration PR.
- Mon 3/8: ACME devs run internal smoke tests and share latency traces.

I've attached a slightly updated plan (redwood-poc-mplan-v2.pdf) and the security Q&A again. Neha / Rishi — if you want to add more low-level tuning tips (quantization, batching) please add below.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. Confirming the following from ACME side:
- Dev owners: Priya N. and Lukas M. will own the integration (I'll introduce them on Monday).
- Timeline: Priya/Lukas start 3/8, smoke tests by 3/12, full test run 3/15-3/29.
- Security: we'll review the attached acme-security-qna.xlsx and come back with any follow-ups by 3/9.

A couple of quick technical notes/questions:
- Webhook delivery: can we configure webhook retries to include a jitter window? We prefer jitter + exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd on our endpoint.
- Streaming: do you provide a sequence number with each token event so we can detect missing fragments on client reconnect?

If those are supported, we are good to proceed with the hosted POC keys. Please send the keys and SDK repo link when available.
